metadata.note: Yes -- Traverse City had passenger rail well before 1900. The Grand Rapids and Indiana Railroad (GR&I) built its main line north from Grand Rapids in stages (Cedar Springs by Dec 1867, Big Rapids by Oct 1870, on toward Petoskey by Nov 1873, reaching Mackinaw City by July 1882). A branch built by the Traverse City Rail Road Company split off the main line at Walton Junction and reached Traverse City in December 1872, with passenger and freight service beginning November 15 1872 -- nearly three decades before 1900. GR&I bought the Traverse City Railroad outright in 1917; GR&I itself was a longtime Pennsylvania Railroad subsidiary. Unlike most other lines on this map, this one has no Amtrak continuation and much of the physical route no longer carries active freight either -- large stretches were converted to the White Pine Trail rail-trail. Geometry is real-traced combining OpenStreetMap's active-rail geometry with the White Pine Trail and Traverse Area Recreational Trail (TART) rail-trail geometry, which together cover almost the entire route from Grand Rapids to Traverse City. The exact location used for 'Walton Junction' is an estimate (the source material didn't give precise coordinates), so the route through that area is approximate.
sources: https://groundworkcenter.org/how-the-railroads-raised-traverse-city/ (Traverse City Rail Road Company branch from Walton Junction finished Dec 1872; passenger/freight service began Nov 15 1872; by 1909 the branch also served Northport and towns in between)

https://www.american-rails.com/gri.html (GR&I main line: Grand Rapids-Cedar Springs opened Dec 25 1867; extended to Big Rapids Oct 1 1870; Paris-Petoskey completed Nov 25 1873; extended to Mackinaw City July 3 1882, 529 route-miles total; longtime Pennsylvania Railroad subsidiary; no Amtrak continuation, much of the route now the White Pine Trail rail-trail)
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Exact frequency/timetable for any era; precise location of Walton Junction; the later Grand Rapids & Indiana / Pennsylvania Railroad passenger service era in detail (e.g. the PRR's Northern Arrow, 1935-1961, which ran Mackinaw City-Cincinnati and likely used this same line, but exact routing through Traverse City itself vs. bypassing it is unconfirmed).
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap (via Overpass API): railway=rail ways tagged usage=main or usage=branch, combined with railway=abandoned cycleway/footway/path ways named 'White Pine Trail' and 'Traverse Area Recreational Trail' -- these two rail-trails cover most of this route's real historic alignment
